description: Core library for detecting LLM-generated "sloppy" code patterns in .NET projects. Use this library to build custom detection rules, IDE extensions, or integrate slopwatch into your own analysis pipelines.
releaseNotes:
**Features:**
* New rule **SW021 — Dynamic Keyword Ban**. Flags any use of the `dynamic` keyword at error severity. Dynamic bypasses compile-time type checking, defeats static analysis, breaks trimming/AOT, and is a common LLM escape hatch for silencing type errors instead of fixing them (#139)
* Generated code is now skipped by default — files with an `<auto-generated>` header or a generated filename (`*.g.cs`, `*.Designer.cs`, `*.generated.cs`, `*.g.i.cs`, `TemporaryGeneratedFile_*`) are no longer analyzed. These are the same signals Roslyn's analyzers use, so slopwatch skips what the compiler skips (#141)
* `[GeneratedCode]` / `[DebuggerNonUserCode]` attribute detection is available as an opt-in via `generatedCode.detectAttributes`. It is off by default because attribute identity cannot be resolved without a compilation, and a wrong answer would silently drop hand-written findings (#141)
* New `generatedCode` section in `.slopwatch/config.json` with `skip` (default), `analyze`, and `analyzeAndReport` modes. `init` and `analyze` both honor it (#141)
* Generated filename patterns (`*.g.cs`, `*.Designer.cs`, `*.generated.cs`, `*.g.i.cs`) are no longer in the default exclude list — the `generatedCode` mode now owns that decision, so `analyze` mode can reach those files (#141)
* `analyzeAndReport` findings carry `isGeneratedCode` in JSON output and a `[generated]` marker in console output (#141)
* `--update-baseline` now preserves baseline entries for files skipped entirely as generated code, so changing modes later does not resurface a wall of findings. Files that are analyzed with individual generated findings filtered out are pruned normally (#141)

**Behavior Changes:**
* **SW021 is on by default at error severity, and there is no way to disable a rule.** There is no rule-filter flag and no config key for rule enablement — only `[SlopwatchSuppress]` or baselining. Combined with `--fail-on error` (the default) and hook mode failing on warnings, **any codebase that uses `dynamic` will start failing CI and blocking edits on upgrade.** If that is not what you want, baseline the existing occurrences before upgrading (#139)
* Generated files that were previously analyzed are now skipped by default. If you rely on findings in generated files, set `generatedCode.mode` to `analyze` or `analyzeAndReport` (#141)
* **Baseline schema is now version 2, and existing baselines must be regenerated.** SW001–SW006 entries used to hash on the display snippet, so two identical occurrences in one file collapsed to a single identity and baselining one silently exempted the other. Entries now hash on a structural path. A version 1 baseline cannot match the new hashes, so `analyze` stops before running and tells you to regenerate (#142):
  ```
  slopwatch init --force
  ```
  Review the regenerated `.slopwatch/baseline.json` before committing it. A baseline with no `version` property at all is treated as version 1 and rejected the same way. If you run `analyze` with a custom `--baseline` path, the error names that path and the remedy becomes `slopwatch init --force --baseline <path>` — `init` now accepts `--baseline` so it can regenerate the file that actually failed. A real migration path — recording which identity scheme produced each entry — is tracked by #107.
* Baseline churn increases: adding or reordering sibling declarations changes the group fingerprint and invalidates those entries. This is deliberate — it rejects false exemptions rather than silently carrying them forward (#142)

**Bug Fixes:**
* Nested git worktrees are now skipped structurally instead of by directory name. The default exclude list contained `**/worktrees/**`, which skipped **any** directory named `worktrees` — including ordinary source — and reported a clean scan for code it never read. A project keeping source under `worktrees/` got `0 files analyzed` and exit 0. Detection now identifies a linked worktree by Git's administrative layout: a `.git` file whose gitdir carries both a `commondir` file and a reciprocal `gitdir` pointer. Submodules and `git init --separate-git-dir` checkouts also use `.git` files but carry neither, so their source is analyzed (#99, #158)
* SW021 no longer flags `using dynamic;` and `using static dynamic;`. A using directive's name is a namespace-or-type reference, never a dynamic-typed slot, so both were false positives. `using D = dynamic;` still reports — that aliases the builtin type and is a genuine dynamic slot (#143)
* SW001 no longer reports a method in the active `#else` or `#elif` branch of an `#if false` block as disabled (#142)
* `[SlopwatchSuppress]` now works on lambdas. It was silently ignored because the suppression checker had no lambda case (#139)
* `[SlopwatchSuppress]` is now valid on `struct`, `interface`, `constructor`, `delegate`, `event`, `enum`, destructor, indexer, operator, conversion operator, local function, and accessor. These were compile errors before (#139)
* `init --config` now forwards the config path to the suppression checker, so suppressions declared in the selected config are honored (#141)
* `init` now honors the `generatedCode` config, so the baseline it writes agrees with the next `analyze` run (#141)

**Performance:**
* SW021 identity generation is now linear in dynamic occurrence count instead of quadratic. Sibling-group fingerprints and structural path segments are memoized per analysis call, so a file with many `dynamic` occurrences no longer rehashes every sibling and rebuilds every ancestor segment per occurrence (#144)
* Structural path caching for SW001–SW006. XML identities dropped from 57 GB to 30 MB at 2,000 findings, and named-method siblings from 3.47 GB / 6.4 s to 2 MB (#142)
* Baseline creation is now linear. `AddEntry` invalidated the hash lookup after every insertion, which was quadratic in entry count (#142)
